Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:

Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Seller Document Review: Departures from Buyer Playbook & Pushback Plan

## Executive Summary
The Seller’s “FINAL” package is **materially misaligned** with our playbook on every core protection: cap, thresholds, time limits, fundamental-title regime, fraud carve-out, disclosure, buyer-knowledge, Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, employee bonuses, Ironquay IP, tax/IP segregation, and title evidence. The “REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE” attempting to pre-classify clauses as [STANDARD] is a tactical ploy; **no clause is closed**. We must issue a comprehensive mark-up and hold firm on all playbook positions.

---

## Detailed Departures & Reasoning

### 1. General Warranty Cap – **Clause 12.1**
- **Seller**: 20% / AUD 4.8M (“STANDARD”).
- **Playbook**: 25% / AUD 6M is starting position; 20% is a *conditional fallback* requiring **written authority from Amelia Frost** (none given).
- **Issue**: Seller treats the fallback as agreed. We have no principal sign-off.
- **Pushback**: Reject 20%; redline to 25% / AUD 6M. Flag that any move to 20% needs Frost written approval *before* we agree.

### 2. Thresholds (De Minimis & Basket) – **Clause 12.2**
- **Seller**: De minimis AUD 25k; basket AUD 250k (excess-only recovery).
- **Playbook**: De minimis AUD 5k; basket AUD 50k (first-dollar liability once exceeded).
- **Issue**: Seller’s thresholds are 5× and 5× wider; excess-only basket shifts risk to Buyer.
- **Pushback**: Redline to playbook figures. No compromise without Frost approval.

### 3. General Claims Period – **Clause 12.3 / 13**
- **Seller**: 18 months; “any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.”
- **Playbook**: 24 months; 18 months is a *fallback needing Frost written approval* (none). Fundamental/Title claims **must** have a separate, longer regime.
- **Issue**: Seller collapses all claims into one short period.
- **Pushback**: Restore 24 months for general claims. Insert standalone Fundamental/Title regime (see §4).

### 4. Fundamental / Title Warranties – **“Fundamental / Title” paragraph**
- **Seller**: Capacity & title warranties subject to **same caps, baskets, time limits** as general warranties.
- **Playbook**: **Separate regime** – 100% cap (AUD 24M), ≥6 years, outside general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- **Issue**: Seller eliminates the fundamental-title protection entirely.
- **Pushback**: New clause: Title/Capacity/Authority = 100% cap, 6-year limitation, no basket/de minimis, no knowledge qualifier. Non-negotiable.

### 5. Fraud / Wilful Concealment / Deliberate Misconduct Carve-Out – **Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5**
- **Seller**: Limitations, exclusive-remedy, non-reliance apply to **“all Claims of any nature.”**
- **Playbook**: Fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct **carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies, non-reliance**. No waiver permitted.
- **Issue**: Seller’s drafting swallows the fraud carve-out.
- **Pushback**: Insert express carve-out clause overriding all limitation provisions. “Nothing in this Agreement limits liability for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct.”

### 6. Disclosure Framework – **Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter §§1.1–1.2**
- **Seller**: General disclosure of **entire data room (DD-002–DD-012) + public registers**.
- **Playbook**: Require **specific, fair disclosure**; reject whole-data-room, public-register, prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Issue**: Seller’s blanket disclosure shifts due-diligence burden to Buyer and undermines warranty protection.
- **Pushback**: Delete general disclosure. Require schedule of *specific* disclosed matters (document, page, paragraph). Reserve rights on any matter not specifically disclosed.

### 7. Buyer Knowledge Exclusion – **Clause 8.3**
- **Seller**: “No claim for any matter of which Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from data room or public records.”
- **Playbook**: **Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions**. Any knowledge qualifier must: (a) name Seller knowledge persons, (b) require reasonable enquiry, (c) never excuse title, capacity, fraud, or specific indemnity.
- **Issue**: Seller’s clause is a total knowledge bar, including constructive knowledge from data room.
- **Pushback**: Strike clause. If Seller insists on knowledge qualifier, limit to *actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals* after reasonable enquiry, and carve out title/capacity/fraud/specific indemnities.

### 8. Bluefen Consent – **Clause 3 / 6.3 / Disclosure Letter §2**
- **Seller**: “Reasonable endeavours”; consent treated as satisfied **on delivery of counterparty’s written consent**. *No final consent or evidence of condition satisfaction in data room.*
- **Playbook**: **Effective consent + evidence conditions satisfied before Completion**. Consent-on-delivery insufficient; reasonable endeavours alone insufficient for material customer.
- **Issue**: ~30% revenue concentration (AUD 3.6M). No certainty consent will be obtained or conditions met.
- **Pushback**: Condition Precedent: (i) executed Bluefen consent, (ii) documentary evidence all Clause 11.3 conditions satisfied. No “reasonable endeavours” fallback. If not met → no Completion.

### 9. Riverlark Facility – **Clause 2 / 7 / Disclosure Letter §3**
- **Seller**: Release to be provided **following Completion** (~AUD 3.2M outstanding).
- **Playbook**: **Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases**. Post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Frost approval.
- **Issue**: Seller leaves ~AUD 3.2M debt and security in place post-Completion; no funded payoff mechanism.
- **Pushback**: Funds flow must show Riverlark payout at Completion (discharge letters, releases). If Seller insists on post-Completion release: irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark + Frost written approval. Otherwise, walk-away right.

### 10. Employee Bonuses (DD-005) – **Funds Flow / Disclosure Letter §5**
- **Seller**: AUD 420k conditional bonuses “matter for the Seller”; **not itemised in funds flow**; on-costs (payroll tax, super) undisclosed.
- **Playbook**: **Specific line item or seller-funded**; funds flow must not silently exclude them. On-costs must be identified and funded.
- **Issue**: Buyer bears hidden post-Completion liability if Seller doesn’t pay.
- **Pushback**: Add funded line item in Completion accounts for AUD 420k + on-costs (grossed up). Alternatively, Seller indemnity for full grossed-up amount payable at Completion.

### 11. Ironquay IP Indemnity – **Clause 11.1 / Disclosure Letter §4**
- **Seller**: Indemnity limited to **SOW3 payment only** (AUD 180k open per DD-010; no independent verification of payment or assignment).
- **Playbook**: **Broaden narrow indemnity**, preserve SOW3 cure; AUD 180k not independently verified either way.
- **Issue**: Indemnity too narrow; payment/assignment unproven.
- **Pushback**: Expand indemnity to cover all IP ownership/encumbrance risks re Ironquay. Require: (a) bank-certified proof of SOW3 payment, (b) executed assignment of Project Materials, (c) survival beyond general cap/basket.

### 12. Export/Privacy Incident (DD-006) – **Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 / Disclosure Letter §6**
- **Seller**: “Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material.” No confirmed breach, scope, access, or notification duty established.
- **Playbook**: Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; **assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand**.
- **Alignment**: Broadly aligned *if* Seller’s “not expected to be material” doesn’t become a representation.
- **Pushback**: Add covenant: Seller must (i) preserve all logs/evidence, (ii) continue investigation, (iii) provide weekly written updates until Completion, (iv) indemnify for any resulting liability (outside general cap). No representation that matter is immaterial.
